subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject media-output provider model refs in chat/session runtime with a clear diagnostic, or add a first-class output-modality contract that routes them through media generation?
rationale: Both paths change public provider/model semantics: rejection improves UX now but needs a way to identify output-only models, while first-class support requires broader provider, tool, response, and channel contracts.

options.title: Diagnostic-first contract
options.body: Treat media-output models as unsupported chat/session models for now, add clear errors/docs, and leave generation on `image_generate`/`video_generate`.

options.title: First-class media-output models
options.body: Add output modality metadata and route image/video-output refs through media generation with channel delivery support.

options.title: Defer to provider plugins
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged until a Poe or generic media provider plugin proves the missing API surface.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic-first contract
recommendation.body: Treat media-output models as unsupported chat/session models for now, add clear errors/docs, and leave generation on `image_generate`/`video_generate`.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent adjacent provider/config work make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
